The main proposal is to **“buy time” by slowing AGI research and reducing competitive race dynamics**, through stronger safety and governance teams at AI labs, coordination between labs and outside safety researchers, and lab safety standards (https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/bkpZHXMJx3dG5waA7/ways-to-buy-time). The mechanism is to **extend development timelines and constrain unsafe deployment**—for example, requiring systems to pass interpretability or deception checks before deployment (https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/bkpZHXMJx3dG5waA7/ways-to-buy-time).

A complementary proposal is to improve the broader understanding of AI capabilities and how they are changing (https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/fRSj2W4Fjje8rQWm9/thoughts-on-sharing-information-about-language-model). This would reduce surprises and underestimation of risks, helping developers adopt adequate precautions and policymakers respond appropriately, rather than mistakenly assuming existing safeguards are sufficient (https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/fRSj2W4Fjje8rQWm9/thoughts-on-sharing-information-about-language-model).
